To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) inhalation exposure to 1,3-butadiene (BD), a chemical used in the production of synthetic rubber, induced an increase in transgene mutant and somatic cell mutation frequency in the mouse bone marrow; (2) the mutational spectrum of BD was A:T base pair mutations; (3) the frequency of somatic cell mutation in the mouse bone was not dependent upon the length of exposure to BD.
1,3 butadiene is mutagenic in the bone marrow in vivo and that the spectrum of mutation is consistent with that expected from a chemical that generates reactive oxygen species and/or DNA adducts.
